workflow.faq_title: Frequently asked questions about n8n implementation

faq.q: How much does an n8n implementation cost?
faq.a: The price of n8n implementation depends on the number of processes and integrations - a single workflow starts at $1,475. I'll give you an exact quote after we talk through your systems.

faq.q: How is n8n different from Zapier?
faq.a: n8n is an open-source alternative to Zapier - it can be self-hosted, which lowers the cost at high volume and gives you full control over your data.

faq.q: Do I need an n8n specialist, or can I build it myself?
faq.a: Simple automations can be built on your own. I step in as an n8n consultant when a process spans several systems, needs error handling, or requires an integration with no ready-made connector.

faq.q: Can n8n be self-hosted?
faq.a: Yes - it's one of n8n's main advantages over Zapier. I set up an instance on your server or in a secure EU cloud and handle maintenance, updates and monitoring as part of ongoing care.

faq.q: Do you migrate automations from Zapier, Make or Power Automate?
faq.a: Yes. I rebuild your existing scenarios in n8n step by step, test them against the same data as the original, and switch over only once the results match - no downtime for the process.

ai.s1_p2: It doesn't replace the expert in your company. It takes the first pass at a large volume of data - documents, messages, questions - and only passes forward what actually needs a human decision.
ai.s1_p3: I start with one well-defined task - a single document type or one category of questions. Once that runs reliably, we widen the scope.

ai.faq_title: Frequently asked questions about n8n AI agents

faq.q: Do I need to be on n8n already?
faq.a: No. If you're not using n8n yet, I set it up as part of the project - self-hosted or cloud, whichever fits your data policy.

faq.q: How is this different from just using the AI Agent node in n8n?
faq.a: The node is the building block. The work is everything around it: choosing a task worth automating, wiring in the right tools and data, handling errors, and testing against real cases so it behaves predictably in production.

faq.q: Can the agent run entirely on our own infrastructure?
faq.a: Yes. With a self-hosted n8n instance and a model you control, no data leaves your environment - this is the usual setup where GDPR or client contracts require it.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: A simple agent wired into one process is ready in 2-3 weeks. A deployment with its own knowledge base and several integrations takes 4-6 weeks.

opieka.selfhost_title: Self-hosted n8n: VPS, Docker and what it actually costs
opieka.selfhost_p1: n8n Community Edition is free, and it runs happily on a small VPS - usually €5-20/month for the server itself. With the official Docker image and docker-compose you can have an instance up in an afternoon. That part is genuinely cheap and well documented, and if you enjoy running it yourself, you should.
opieka.selfhost_p2: The cost shows up later: an upgrade that changes how a node behaves, an expired TLS certificate, a container that came back up with an empty queue, a workflow that stopped silently after a vendor changed their API. On a self-managed box you find out when someone notices the data is missing. That is the part I take over - the server can stay yours, but somebody is actually watching it.

case_study.after: Monitoring catches the error within minutes, the team gets notified, and the fix ships the same day.
case_study.result: Time-to-detect dropped from days to minutes, zero lost orders from silent integration failures.

faq.q: Do you have to have built the automation to take over its care?
faq.a: No. I also take over care for automations built earlier by someone else, after reviewing them first.

faq.q: What happens if I cancel the care plan?
faq.a: The automation keeps running, but nobody responds when something breaks after a change in one of the connected systems.

faq.q: What's the difference between Standard and Pro care?
faq.a: Standard means monitoring with a response time of up to 48h. Pro means a 4h SLA, priority in the queue, and a monthly report.

faq.q: Is n8n hosting GDPR-compliant?
faq.a: Yes - I run automations on a self-hosted server in the EU, without passing data to any party outside the agreed processing chain.

faq.q: What's the best VPS for n8n?
faq.a: For most 5-50 person companies a 2 vCPU / 4 GB VPS in the EU handles n8n plus its Postgres database, with headroom for queue mode later. What matters more than the provider is backups, monitoring and a restore you have actually tested - which is usually what's missing on a DIY box.

faq.q: Can I just run n8n on Docker myself?
faq.a: Yes - n8n ships official Docker images and a docker-compose setup, and for a personal instance that's perfectly fine. It becomes a problem once the automation carries real business processes and nobody's job is to notice that it stopped.

faq.q: Is n8n Community Edition enough, or do I need a paid plan?
faq.a: For most of the implementations I do, self-hosted Community Edition is enough. Paid tiers matter mainly for SSO, granular permissions and multi-environment setups - I'll tell you plainly if your case actually needs them.

faq.q: What does n8n hosting cost in total?
faq.a: The server itself is typically €5-20/month. Managed hosting with monitoring and updates starts at $100/month, and full care with an SLA from $225/month - the difference is who is responsible when it breaks at 7am.

ksef_intl_page.h1: KSeF E-Invoicing for Foreign Companies in Poland
ksef_intl_page.subtitle: Poland's national e-invoicing system (KSeF) is now mandatory. If your company has a Polish VAT registration, branch or subsidiary, I connect your accounting system to KSeF and automate the invoice workflow around it.
ksef_intl_page.service_type: KSeF e-invoicing compliance for foreign entities

who.title: Foreign parent companies with a Polish subsidiary or branch
who.desc: Your Polish entity issues and receives invoices under Polish law, whether or not the rest of the group operates there.

who.title: International groups centralizing finance operations
who.desc: You run invoicing and accounting from a shared services center outside Poland, and need one team to handle the Polish leg without hiring locally.

who.title: Companies running non-Polish accounting software
who.desc: SAP, NetSuite, Xero or anything else - KSeF doesn't care what you use internally, but it does require a bridge to its own API.

requirements: Every invoice issued to a Polish counterparty must be submitted in KSeF's fixed structured XML format (FA schema), not as a PDF or paper document.
Authentication happens via a qualified electronic signature or a NIP-based token - foreign companies need a Polish NIP to authenticate at all.
API sessions and request limits apply at volume - without monitoring, a session can silently drop mid-batch.
Invoices that still arrive by email or paper alongside KSeF need to be reconciled and deduplicated, not double-booked.
solutions: Connect KSeF's API directly to whatever accounting or ERP system your company already uses, without switching platforms.
Automate invoice submission and retrieval, so your finance team stops manually re-entering data into KSeF.
Handle deduplication between KSeF and any invoices still arriving through other channels.
Monitor API sessions and limits, with an alert before a batch fails instead of after.

case_study.title: German manufacturing group, Polish subsidiary
case_study.before: The Polish subsidiary's invoices were manually re-entered into KSeF by a local bookkeeper, disconnected from the group's SAP system in Germany.
case_study.after: Automation pushes invoices from SAP into KSeF's API directly and pulls incoming invoices back into the subsidiary's ledger.
case_study.result: The local bookkeeper's manual KSeF workload dropped to occasional exception handling only.

ksef_intl_page.pricing_text: The KSeF integration package (API connection, deduplication, monitoring) starts at $3,225. Ongoing support starts at $225/month. A typical implementation takes 2-4 weeks.

faq.q: Does my foreign company need to comply with KSeF?
faq.a: If you have a Polish VAT registration, branch, or subsidiary issuing invoices to Polish counterparties, KSeF compliance applies to you the same way it applies to Polish companies.

faq.q: Can KSeF connect to non-Polish accounting software?
faq.a: Yes - KSeF exposes a REST API. I build the bridge between your existing system (SAP, NetSuite, Xero, or anything else) and KSeF, so you don't have to switch accounting platforms.

faq.q: We already have a Polish bookkeeper handling this manually - is automation still worth it?
faq.a: Automation doesn't replace your bookkeeper - it removes the repetitive re-entry work so they can focus on judgment calls and exceptions instead of retyping invoices.

faq.q: Do you work remotely, or do you need to be on-site in Poland?
faq.a: Everything I described here is done remotely - the API integration and monitoring don't require anyone on-site.
